title: PARLIAMENT QUESTION: INNOVATION IN SCIENCE PURSUIT FOR INSPIRED RESEARCH (INSPIRE) PROGRAMME
body_text:
Over the last five years, the Innovation in Science Pursuit for Inspired Research (INSPIRE) Programme of the department of science and technology has systematically nurtured scientific talent at different stages of the academic and research pipeline through its four major components. INSPIRE MANAK (Million Minds Augmenting National Aspiration and Knowledge) promotes innovation and scientific creativity among students aged 10-17 years (Classes VI-XII) by encouraging them to develop and showcase original ideas and innovations. INSPIRE Scholarship for Higher Education (SHE) supports meritorious students aged 17-22 years pursuing undergraduate and postgraduate studies in natural and basic sciences by awarding 12,000 scholarships annually, each valued at ₹80,000 per year. INSPIRE Fellowship encourages outstanding graduates and INSPIRE scholars to pursue research through full-time Ph.D. programme(s) by providing financial support up to five years, including a fellowship of ₹37,000 per month as Junior Research Fellow (JRF), ₹42,000 per month as Senior Research Fellow (SRF), admissible House Rent Allowance (HRA), and an annual contingency grant of ₹20,000. INSPIRE Faculty Fellowship supports outstanding postdoctoral researchers, generally in the 27-32 years age group (with applicable age relaxations for reserved categories), through a five-year fellowship. Fellows receive ₹1,25,000 per month, an annual increment of ₹2,000, and a research grant of ₹35 lakh over the fellowship period.
The Government has been committed to promotion of the Innovation in Science Pursuit for Inspired Research (INSPIRE) Programme to encourage meritorious students to pursue higher education and research in science. The component-wise INSPIRE activities during the last five years, including the number of students and young researchers supported under each component, are provided below:
Program/Financial Year 2021-22 2022-23 2023-24 2024-25 2025-26 INSPIRE-MANAK 52720 43381 46926 50009 49805 INSPIRE-SHE 18039 19771 18236 20354 24276 INSPIRE Fellowship 2768 2872 2811 2448 3364 INSPIRE Faculty Fellowship 474 338 299 225 477
With a goal to enhance innovative research by the young generation in the country, impact of these components is being monitored and analysed to facilitate their strategic planning.
(d) The Government has undertaken a series of targeted interventions to significantly expand the outreach and inclusivity of INSPIRE Programme, with a special focus on rural, remote and aspirational districts across the country. These efforts include extensively deep dissemination of information through State Education Departments, District Education Officers, schools and digital platforms; organization of awareness campaigns, orientation programmes, webinars, and capacity-building workshops for teachers and school authorities to improve the quality and reach of nominations; and the conduct of District, State, and National Level Exhibition and Project Competitions (DLEPCs, SLEPCs, and NLEPCs) to identify, recognize and nurture innovative ideas among school students. To further strengthen the innovation ecosystem, mentorship programmes have been organized in collaboration with premier institutions such as IITs, NITs, IISERs, and other leading scientific organizations, providing selected students with guidance on prototype development, innovation, and scientific research. These sustained efforts have led to inclusive participation in the INSPIRE programmes spanning various regions across the country, sections of our society.
A growing number of students from rural and remote districts have benefited through innovation grants, mentoring support, and opportunities to showcase their scientific talent on national platforms. Collectively, these interventions have strengthened the scientific temper and culture of inquiry, fostered grassroots innovation, expanded equitable access to science education, scholarships and research fellowships and broadened the pipeline of young scientific talent from most regions of the country.
This information was given by the Minister of State (Ind. Charge) Science & Technology; Earth Sciences and Minister of State PMO; Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions; Department of Atomic Energy and Space Dr. Jitendra Singh in a written reply in Lok Sabha today.

NKR/FT

enrichment.summary: In a written Lok Sabha reply, the Minister of State for Science & Technology Dr. Jitendra Singh detailed the INSPIRE programme's four components - MANAK, SHE, Fellowship, and Faculty Fellowship - which support students and researchers from school level to postdoctoral research. Data for 2021-22 to 2025-26 showed INSPIRE-MANAK supporting around 43,000-53,000 students annually, SHE scholarships rising from 18,039 to 24,276, PhD Fellowships around 2,400-3,400, and Faculty Fellowships between 225-477 annually. The reply also outlined outreach efforts targeting rural, remote and aspirational districts through awareness campaigns, exhibitions, and mentorship with IITs, NITs and IISERs.
enrichment.context:
INSPIRE (Innovation in Science Pursuit for Inspired Research) is a flagship scheme of the Department of Science and Technology (DST) launched in 2008 to attract talented youth into science and build a strong human resource base for research and development in India. It is structured as a pipeline covering four life stages: school students (MANAK), undergraduate/postgraduate scholars (SHE), doctoral researchers (Fellowship), and postdoctoral faculty (Faculty Fellowship), reflecting a continuum approach to nurturing scientific talent rather than one-off interventions. This is significant in the context of India's persistently low Gross Expenditure on R&D (GERD) as a percentage of GDP and concerns about brain drain and declining interest in pure sciences among students who often gravitate toward professional courses like engineering and medicine.

The scheme's focus on rural, remote and aspirational districts ties into broader government priorities such as the Aspirational Districts Programme and efforts to democratize access to science education and research funding beyond urban, elite institutions. Programmes like DLEPCs/SLEPCs/NLEPCs (District/State/National Level Exhibitions and Project Competitions) mirror the format of the National Children's Science Congress and other talent-search mechanisms, aiming to identify grassroots innovation. INSPIRE data and monitoring also feed into larger national science policy discussions, including the Science, Technology and Innovation Policy (STIP) and efforts to increase the number of PhDs and researchers per capita, an area where India lags behind countries like the US, China, and South Korea.

prelims_questions.question:
The INSPIRE programme of the Department of Science and Technology includes which of the following components?
1. INSPIRE MANAK
2. INSPIRE SHE
3. INSPIRE Internship
4. INSPIRE Faculty Fellowship

prelims_questions.explanation: As per the release, the four major components of INSPIRE are MANAK, SHE, Fellowship, and Faculty Fellowship. 'INSPIRE Internship' is not mentioned as a component, so the correct combination is MANAK, SHE, and Faculty Fellowship (option with 1, 2 and 4).

prelims_questions.question: Under the INSPIRE Programme, the 'INSPIRE Scholarship for Higher Education (SHE)' is meant for students in which age group?
prelims_questions.explanation: The release states INSPIRE SHE supports meritorious students aged 17-22 years pursuing undergraduate and postgraduate studies in natural and basic sciences.

mains_questions.question: Discuss the significance of talent-nurturing schemes like INSPIRE in strengthening India's scientific research ecosystem. What measures can be taken to ensure equitable participation of students from rural and aspirational districts in such programmes?

mains_questions.question: India continues to lag behind developed nations in terms of Gross Expenditure on Research and Development (GERD) and the density of researchers. Analyze the role of government scholarship and fellowship schemes in addressing this gap, citing suitable examples.
